purpose: Candidate-authored input-only test inputs for the D-M06-A JCS review; carries no answers, no anticipated results, and no grading information. The later authorized witness, if any, supplies its own outcomes.
input_convention: Each fixture's 'input' is raw JSON text exactly as a candidate implementation would receive it, so text-level cases (escapes, duplicate names) are representable alongside structural ones.

fixtures.note: Flat object with ASCII keys out of alphabetical order.
Nested object inside array inside object.
Ordinary string values with spaces, punctuation, and digits.
Key order: escaped-accent key vs plain key that sorts before it in raw form.
Key order: supplementary-plane key (U+1D400) vs U+FFFF key; UTF-16 code-unit order and code-point order disagree on this pair.
Text-level \u escapes that denote the same parsed strings as literal spellings, given as array elements so no object-name collision is implied.
Composed vs decomposed accents: canonically equivalent, visually identical, distinct code-point sequences.
C0 control characters via JSON short escapes and the \u00xx range, plus quote and backslash.
Non-ASCII characters emitted verbatim: CJK, emoji (supplementary plane), Nordic letters.
Number edges: zero and negative zero, plain decimal, smallest subnormal, near-max double.
Number edges at exponent and precision thresholds cited in the draft: 1e21 boundary, 1e-6 and 1e-7, 2^53-1, 2^53, 2^53+1.
Long integer literal with more significant digits than a double holds.
Text-level duplicate property names: the draft proposes the domain bound rejects this input.
Text-level lone surrogate escape (\\udead): the draft proposes the domain bound terminates on this input.
Sorting stress: keys that collide after unescaping share one parsed name; plus 1-character and multi-character shared-prefix keys.
